content.comment_body: Hello everyone, I'm planning a home automation project and chose [product_name] as my PLC. My setup involves using pulse relays to activate circuits; when the pulse switch is triggered, the relay (finder 13.81) toggles and changes the circuit state. My thought was to wire an output from [product_name] in parallel with the switch to automate the process. I'm not a professional engineer, but I have a good grasp of electrical concepts. Do you foresee any problems with this configuration? Is there any risk of damaging my [product_name]? Appreciate any advice.
This solution will work. As your [product_name] has relay dry output contacts, your wiring simply adds another contact in parallel with the current switch.

There’s a challenge here. How will [product_name] determine if the light is actually on or off? You’ll need some form of feedback; otherwise, manual switching can cause the control logic to become out of sync with the actual device status.

analysis.insight_summary: Users explored integrating [product_name] into a home automation setup by paralleling its outputs with manual pulse switches that control relays. One user validated the wiring approach, but another raised a concern about system feedback: without external indicators, [product_name] cannot reliably track the current state if operated manually, leading to possible mismatches between control intent and device state.
analysis.user_expectations: The user anticipates installing [product_name] alongside existing pulse switches without causing hardware issues, and expects it to reliably command the circuit even with manual intervention.
